'''''Cylindropuntia whipplei''''' (formerly known as ''Opuntia whipplei'', common name '''Whipple cholla''') is a member of the cactus family, [[Cactaceae]].

== Usage ==
The [[Zuni people]] rub the spines off the fruit and then dry them for winter use. The dried fruit is also ground into a flour, mixed with ground corn meal and made into a mush.<ref>{{cite book |author=Matilda Coxe Stevenson |year=1915 |title=Ethnobotany of the Zuni Indians |publisher=SI-BAE Annual Report #30 |page=69}}</ref> Spineless fruits are eaten raw or stewed.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Castetter, Edward F. |year=1935 |title=Ethnobiological studies in the American Southwest I. Uncultivated native plants used as sources of food |journal=University of New Mexico Bulletin |volume=4 |issue=1 |pages=1–44}}</ref>
